statement: Substitute notice of a data breach is available when the business demonstrates that the cost of providing notice would exceed $250,000, that the affected class exceeds 500,000 persons, or that it lacks sufficient contact information; substitute notice consists of email notice when the business holds an email address for the subject persons, conspicuous posting of the notice on the business's internet website page for a minimum of 30 days, and notification to major statewide media (Civil Code § 1798.82(j)(3)).
caveat: Text current as of January 1, 2026. Substitute notice is a permitted method of delivery, and the 30-calendar-day disclosure deadline in § 1798.82(a)(2)(A) governs timing separately. The demonstration of cost, class size, or missing contact information is the notifying business's to make. This repo does not choose a notice method.
